top_stories.ai_overview: Artificial Intelligence Build efficient agents with knowledge distillation on Amazon SageMaker AI You built a shopping assistant on a frontier model, and it works. A shopper asks for “a black waist bag under twenty dollars from a shop with at least 4.5 stars,” and the agent searches the catalog, inspects candidates, checks the constraints, and commits to a recommendation.
top_stories.ai_what_happened: But what does that interaction actually cost?
ai_key_details: An agentic assistant is not one model call, it is a loop: search, read results, refine, verify, decide.
A single completed task can be multiple calls to that frontier model, and you pay for every one, on every shopper.

top_stories.ai_whats_new: The catch is quality: a smaller model usually falls short on the task, which is why the larger one was chosen in the first place.
ai_key_takeaways: At production scale, that per-task cost compounds, erodes the project’s ROI, and stops the project from shipping.

Knowledge distillation closes that gap by transferring the behavior of the larger “teacher” model into a smaller “student”, training the student to reproduce the teacher’s outputs, so it keeps much of the quality at the smaller model’s speed and cost.
In this post you will learn how to use knowledge distillation, and specifically sequence-level knowledge distillation (SeqKD), to fine-tune a shopping agent on Amazon SageMaker AI.

top_stories.ai_overview: In recent months, we’ve made substantial progress on reducing the effectiveness of distillation attacks on Claude using new methods, as we outline in this blog. Early evidence suggests that these methods have reduced the amount of data harvested by distillers by around 90 to 99%.
top_stories.ai_what_happened: Distillation attacks are covert, industrial-scale campaigns to extract the capabilities of one model and replicate them in another, without the authorization of the original model’s developers.
ai_key_details: They are often conducted using networks of fraudulent accounts.
These attacks allow companies to mimic frontier capabilities for a fraction of the development time and cost.
Zhipu, for example, distilled the cyber capabilities of leading US models during the development of GLM-5.3.
The US Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence (CAISSI) has since assessed GLM-5.3 to be the most cyber-capable open-weights model released to date.
top_stories.ai_why_it_matters: First, distillation enables companies to build models that approach the capability frontier, but which have, in practice, been released without proportionally robust safeguards.
